paper.title_en: Multiple Many-Body Localization Transitions in Driven Non-Hermitian Chains with Spatially Correlated Potentials
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the fate of a many-body-localized phase in a periodically driven non-Hermitian chain of hard-core bosons with directed hopping subject to a binary onsite potential in the form of a deterministic quasiperiodic Fibonacci sequence. While Floquet heating generally results in the thermalization of the many-body-localized system with increasing driving period, our initially many-body-localized phase displays a sequence of localization-delocalization transitions, leaving isolated extended islands between many-body-localized phases. Non-Hermiticity makes these extended islands strongly boundary sensitive, and gives rise to a Floquet many-body skin effect under open boundary conditions. We show that the re-entrant many-body localization~(MBL) is independent of our choice of potential by reproducing this phenomenology when instead considering a potential with a genuinely disordered random-dimer sequence. Furthermore, we find that the directed hopping plays a dual role: it stabilizes MBL in regimes that are only weakly localized in the Hermitian limit, while promoting delocalization and broadening extended regions elsewhere. Our work advances the fundamental understanding of non-Hermitian and nonequilibrium quantum matter by revealing how directed hopping and spatial correlations in the onsite landscape jointly govern MBL in periodically driven interacting systems
